sections.overview: Parachromis managuensis, the Jaguar Cichlid or Jaguar Guapote, is a large freshwater fish native to the Atlantic-draining rivers and lakes of Central America.
sections.identification: It has a large mouth, projecting lower jaw and prominent canine-like teeth. Dark marks along the flank and spots on the fins contribute to its jaguar-like pattern.
sections.habitat: It occurs from the Ulúa River in Honduras south to the Matina River in Costa Rica. Accounts describe lakes, springs and ponds, often over muddy or sandy bottoms.
sections.diet: Adults are strongly fish-eating predators; aquatic invertebrates are an important part of the juvenile diet.
sections.behavior: Both parents guard the eggs and fry. It has also been introduced beyond its native range.
sections.reproduction: It lays batches of eggs on hard surfaces such as rocks, and both parents care for the eggs and young.
sections.ecology: It is one of several cichlids in the genus Parachromis. Effects on ecosystems where it is introduced remain uncertain.
sections.conservation: FishBase reports a global IUCN assessment of Least Concern from 2020.
